     Star-fish. Radiata.

     Used by Hippocrates, and others, in uterine diseases. See Aldrovandi, Frankf. edition, 1623, p. 298.

     Brauns had given it homœopathically since 1835. Petroz proved and introduced it, by publishing his provings on seven persons and cured cases in the Journ. de la Soc. Gallicane, in 1850-51. It was translated into English in 1852, by Metcalf, and into German by Brückner. A valuable proving was made in 1853, by Dr. Günther, of a tincture of the sea-star, caught in Newport, and prepared by the late Dr. Geist, of Boston ; other provings we have by Berridge, in London, and Macfarlan, in Philadelphia. Douglas has given characteristics. It has not been used often, but in cases of the highest importance.

Itching : upon chest ; in right axilla ; around thumb nail ; below left knee ; on right tibia ; on thighs and legs.
Dryness : in throat.
Heat : in head ; in eyes ; in throat ; in rectum ; in urethra ; in feet.
Coldness : in left arm.
   

SKIN. [46] [Aster.]
Itching spots.
Furfuraceous eruption between mamma and on left olecranon.
Chronic cutaneous affections and old ulcers with stinking ichor.
Eruption on thighs and insteps of small itching vesicles which tear easily and form superficial ulcers.
Scrofulous ulcer left side of throat.
Itch.
Tetters.
Sensitive edges, fetid discharge. θ Cancer mamma.
Dry, harsh skin, earthy appearance. θ Cancer mamma.
Eruption of small blisters on thighs and legs, itching on ankles, changing to small burning ulcers, spreading but remaining superficial.
Skin destitute of pliability and elasticity. θ Ulcer on neck.
   

STAGE OF LIFE, CONSTITUTION. [47] [Aster.]
Sycosis.
Flabby, lymphatic constitution.
Girl, æt. 22, delicate, lymphatic and very irritable temperament ; epilepsy.
Woman, æt. 48, flabby, lymphatic constitution, for several years a scrofulous ulcer.
Man, æt. 56, plethoric constitution, sedentary since eight years ; epilepsy.
A woman, æt. 56, dry constitution ; scirrhus in breast.
Woman, æt. 60, strong constitution ; induration of left mamma.
A man, æt. 74, nervous, sanguine, suffering hardships of war as an officer, particularly during campaign in Egypt ; threatened apoplexy.
   

RELATIONS. [48] [Aster.]
Antidotes to Ast. rub. : Plumbum and Zincum.
Side relations : Murex., Sepia.
Compare : Crot. tig., Grat., Gummi gut., Jatrop., Thuya (all similar in diarrhœa) ; Bellad. (pains come and go suddenly) ; Lilium tig. (sexual desire increased in women).
Useful after : Bellad., Carbo an., Conium and Silic. (in scirrhus of mamma) ; Sulphur, Bellad., Calc. carb. (in epilepsy).
Incompatibles : coffee and Nux vom.
Ipecac. relieved after Nux vom. aggravated.
